articles.headline: Fantasy basketball: Sleepers, breakouts and busts for 2026-27
articles.description: Which fantasy basketball players are going to exceed expectations in 2026-27? Who will disappoint? Who is ready to take things to an elite level? Our experts list their picks.
articles.body:
Putting together a winning fantasy basketball roster starts with a great draft. And to have a great draft, you need to know which players to go after and which to avoid.

So which players will out-produce their average draft position (ADP) this season? Who will take their game to another level? And which players are the biggest risk to take a step backward?

Our fantasy basketball experts André Snellings, Eric Moody, Eric Karabell, Jim McCormick, Steve Alexander and Michael F. Florio offer their top sleepers, breakouts and busts for the 2026-27 NBA season.

Sleepers

Sleeper: A player who will far surpass his average draft position (ADP) in standard ESPN leagues.

Naz Reid, C/PF, Charlotte Hornets

Snellings: Reid was the NBA Sixth Man of the Year two seasons ago and had carved out a role with the Timberwolves as essentially a starter that had to come off the bench due to the depth of frontline talent in Minnesota. With his trade to the Hornets, Reid has the opportunity to show that he can produce even more as a full-time starter. Reid is an efficient scorer, a strong rebounder and defender, and one of the best 3-point shooting big men in the league. Particularly in category leagues, he is poised to return fantasy value far beyond where is selected in most drafts.

Alexander: Reid has always been one of my favorite under-the-radar players and he'll have new life this season, hopefully starting for the Hornets. I wish he was a better free throw shooter (72.8% for his career), but he only shot 1.6 of them per game last year, meaning the low volume won't hurt you too bad in that category. I expect all of his numbers to get a boost this year and he's played between 68 and 81 games in six straight seasons. The only concern is his usage rate while playing alongside Coby White, Kon Knueppel and Brandon Miller, but there should be enough to go around for Reid to eat.

Julius Randle, PF, Brooklyn Nets

Karabell: Randle's numbers and fantasy value fell quite a bit during two seasons with the Timberwolves, especially in rebounds, but there is little holding him back from high usage and big fantasy value with the barren Nets. Look at what Randle achieved statistically during his Knicks seasons, and expect a return to at least 24 PPG, 10 RPG and 5 APG for the other New York team, easily outproducing his tepid ADP, which always seemed out of line with his actual production.

Caleb Wilson, SF, Chicago Bulls

Florio: The No. 4 overall pick in this years NBA draft hit the ground running this summer. Wilson averaged 23.5 points, 7.3 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 2.5 blocks per game in the Summer League. That is after putting up similar numbers at North Carolina last year. He has apparently been turning heads in workouts with LeBron James, too. He will start at power forward on a Bulls team that has lots of opportunities up for grabs, both in terms of scoring and rebounding. articles.description: All of the important fantasy spin and actionable takeaways resulting from the latest baseball news.
articles.body:
Everything that happens in and around MLB has some additional context when viewed from a fantasy baseball perspective. From lineup changes to minor league call-ups to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values in fantasy baseball.

Our fantasy baseball buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around MLB.

Sept. 22: Tuesday's news to know

By Todd Zola

Tuesday's schedule gets an early start with a doubleheader in the Bronx between the New York Yankees and Tampa Bay Rays. The opener gets underway at 1:05 p.m. ET, with the nightcap being part of the 15-game evening slate. The AL East combatants both have seven games left, with the Rays six games ahead of the Yankees. Winning just one game assures the Rays of winning the division and the No. 1 seed in the American League.

Yesterday, the Chicago Cubs announced that 3B Alex Bregman will miss the rest of the regular season. He was diagnosed with facial fractures after being hit in the side of his face with a foul ball while getting loose in the on-deck circle on Saturday. The veteran does not require surgery, so he may still return to help the club in the playoffs. More will be revealed about his status later in the week.

The Baltimore Orioles pulled C Samuel Basallo from last night's game in the seventh inning. He was hit in the mask with a foul ball earlier in the contest, then was hit a few times with foul tips. The rookie has been the club's main backstop for just over a month, but he's batting just .158/.244/.250 over 25 games during that span. Carlos Narvaez will see more action if Basallo remains out.

In the same contest, Toronto Blue Jays outfielder Brett Bateman exited early due to a sore right hip. X-rays were negative, leaving his status as day-to-day. The 24-year-old outfielder is hitting a surprising .322/.393/.416, though with only two homers and three steals over 37 games. The Blue Jays were already playing without Vladimir Guerrero Jr. thanks to lower-back tightness. He is also day-to-day, with Sean Keys filling in at first base.

The Detroit Tigers placed Colt Keith on the 10-day IL yesterday, ending his season. The infielder's .258/.322/.406 final line mirrors last year's effort, with a tad less power but a few more stolen bases.

Reinforcements are returning for the Los Angeles Dodgers, with Andy Pages and Roki Sasaki both set to be activated before tonight's home date with the San Diego Padres. Pages is expected to be reinserted as the regular center fielder, shifting Tommy Edman to the keystone. Pages was out for over a month following surgery on a broken bone in his left hand. articles.headline: Seven things Solak thinks entering NFL Week 3
articles.description: Can Baker Mayfield rebound? Are the Chargers doomed? Is the Eagles' new offense actually encouraging for Jalen Hurts? Get ready for Week 3 with seven takes.
articles.body:
Week 2 is in the books! It came with big upsets (Raiders over Chargers! Browns over Bucs!) and devastating injuries (such as Commanders QB Jayden Daniels and Giants QB Jaxson Dart). Week 3 feels as murky a future week as ever.

Every Tuesday of the NFL season, I'll turn the page from the previous week to the upcoming one with seven things I think. These aren't full-scale predictions; those come later in the week. They aren't concrete takeaways from the past week of NFL action, either; those are fired off Sunday or Monday. Instead, these are the uncertain topics. They are things that might be true, but it'll probably take the next few games to find out. And at the bottom, you'll find a few extra half-thoughts ... just those little inklings I'm unable to shake.

This week, I'm starting with my concern for a big-ticket quarterback contract signed not even a month ago, my concern for one key AFC contender and my lack of concern for two others. Here are seven things I think ahead of Week 3.

Jump to:

Bucs regret the Mayfield deal

Chargers to pick top-10 in 2027

Patriots offense is fine, everyone

Hurts is settling into Eagles' offense

Jaguars trenches will be postseason downfall

Henry won't solve Ravens' late-game issues

Donald's workout regimen paid off

Five extra inklings

I think ... the Buccaneers are already regretting that Baker Mayfield deal

Mayfield has not played well through the first two games of the season.

This does not mean he is a bad quarterback who is undeserving of a nice contract. Two game samples are, in a vacuum, barely above meaningless. (They're just meaningful enough that you should keep reading this column.) But it would have been nice to see how this season played out, to see if this two-game trend continued, before signing an extension.

Mayfield and the Buccaneers looked destined for a prove-it season before the Buccaneers "surprised" Mayfield with an eleventh-hour offer that clearly met his expectations. It is a three-year deal, as Mayfield wanted, though it's really a two-year deal with a $55 million team option in 2029. Still, at $55 million per year, Mayfield is making Matthew Stafford and Trevor Lawrence sort of money ... Joe Burrow and Josh Allen sort of money.

Mayfield's play has been decidedly below that level to start the season. Through two weeks, Mayfield is 29th among 32 quarterbacks in EPA per dropback and 27th in success rate. Of course, two-game samples are useless, so let's add last season. Since the start of 2025, Mayfield is 24th among 32 quarterbacks in EPA per dropback and 25th in success rate.

But last season was a down year. Mayfield played through a strained knee that he suffered in Week 2 and endured shoulder pain (non-throwing side) after a big hit in Week 12. His 2025 offensive coordinator, Josh Grizzard, was fired at the end of the season. So, let's throw in 2024 as well. Since the start of that season, Mayfield's career year with offensive coordinator Liam Coen, Mayfield is 13th in EPA

articles.body:
Feyenoord right back Givairo Read has caught the eye of Liverpool, Arsenal and Manchester City, while Manchester United are monitoring Borussia Dortmund striker Serhou Guirassy and Vålerenga's 15-year-old winger Gabriel Rajkovic. Trending rumors

- Liverpool are monitoring Feyenoord right back Givairo Read, but face competition from Arsenal and Manchester City, according to TEAMtalk. The 20-year-old Netherlands U21 international has registered four assists in seven Eredivisie appearances this season, with all three clubs continuing to track his progress following summer interest. A January move remains an option depending on formal approaches, after Nottingham Forest and AS Roma previously submitted offers of around €20 million that came to nothing.

- Manchester United are monitoring Borussia Dortmund striker Serhou Guirassy as they assess attacking options ahead of January, TEAMtalk reports. The 30-year-old is being considered as an experienced option should Joshua Zirkzee depart, while United remain committed to Benjamin Šeško despite his recent injury issues. Dortmund are reluctant to let Guirassy leave, but his contract has than two years remaining, which could force their hand. Meanwhile, The Sun reports that United are targeting Vålerenga's 15-year-old winger Gabriel Rajkovic as a replacement for JJ Gabriel. 

- Barcelona are monitoring Athletico Paranaense center back Arthur Dias, as per Mundo Deportivo. Barca's head of scouting, João Amaral, reportedly watched the 19-year-old against Bahia, with Tottenham Hotspur, Newcastle United and Atlético Madrid also among his admirers. The left-footed defender, who earned a call-up to Carlo Ancelotti's Brazil squad, has a transfer value of around €30 million and after Spurs previously had a €21 million offer for 80% of his economic rights rejected.

- Tottenham Hotspur will not pursue a move for free-agent Mauro Icardi, Football Insider has revealed. The 33-year-old striker has been available since leaving Galatasaray in July, but Spurs are wary of his wage demands and lack of Premier League experience. Serie A is considered the likeliest destination for the former Sampdoria, Inter Milan and PSG star, with Lazio among several interested Italian clubs.

- Roma are interested in signing free-agent Raphaël Guerreiro, according to Tuttomercatoweb. The 32-year-old Portugal international left back has re-emerged as an option for manager Gian Piero Gasperini as a natural left-footed alternative on the flank, while Olympiacos are also interested in the former Bayern Munich defender.

articles.headline: 2026 NFL Power Rankings: How all 32 teams stack up for Week 3
articles.description: How do all 32 NFL teams stack up ahead of Week 3? Plus, what we know for sure about the starting QBs around the league.
articles.body:
Week 2 of the 2026 NFL season marked a return to defensive dominance one week after record scoring numbers. This season, NFL defenses have a 35% pressure percentage (the highest through two weeks since ESPN began tracking pressures in 2009) and a 25% pass rush rush win rate (highest since 2017).

How is this impacting quarterbacks around the league? In our Power Rankings ahead of Week 3, we asked our NFL Nation reporters to name the one thing we've learned so far from each team's QB situation. Which quarterbacks are handling the pressure? How are teams such as the Giants, Bears, Commanders, Seahawks and Vikings dealing with early injuries to their QB1s?

To form the list, our power panel of more than a dozen NFL analysts evaluates how all 32 teams stack up against one another, ranking them from No. 1 to 32. And here are a few highlights from this week's rankings:

The 49ers climbed into the top three, led by a near-perfect two weeks from quarterback Brock Purdy. He became the fifth QB in NFL history to record multiple games with 90% completion percentage, per ESPN Research. And San Francisco gets to stay at home for two more weeks, starting with the Cardinals next Sunday.

The Chargers are down to No. 22 after falling to 0-2. According to ESPN Research, they are the second team in the Super Bowl era (since 1966) to be favored by at least 6.5 points in each of their first two games and lose both. The Raiders, who most recently beat the Chargers, are at No. 20 and 2-0 for the first time since 2021.

Meanwhile, the Falcons and Dolphins are squarely at the bottom of the rankings. The Dolphins are the only team to not lead at any point this season, and ESPN's Football Power Index already gives them a 43% chance at the No. 1 pick. Atlanta is hoping to rebound with quarterback Michael Penix Jr. back in the fold from ACL surgery.

Let's get into the full list, starting with the same No. 1 team as last week.

articles.headline: LaLiga president Javier Tebas dismisses Real Madrid conspiracy claims as a 'smokescreen'
articles.description: LaLiga president Javier Tebas has called claims of a refereeing conspiracy against Real Madrid "a smokescreen to hide other shortcomings" after the team's defeat to Atletico Madrid in Sunday's derby.
articles.body:
LaLiga president Javier Tebas has called claims of a refereeing conspiracy against Real Madrid "a smokescreen to hide other shortcomings" after the team's defeat to Atletico Madrid in Sunday's derby.

Coach José Mourinho said Madrid were denied "two clear red cards" in the game at the Metropolitano -- bringing a printout of photos of the incidents to his post-match news conference -- and alleged referee Miguel Ortiz Arias "couldn't cope with the pressure" of the high-profile fixture due to a lack of experience.

"I don't want to say this was prepared -- I want to think they were mistakes," Mourinho said, after a result which left Madrid six points behind Barcelona in the title race, adding that "if they let us compete on an even playing field, there's a long way left."

Tebas, who has frequently clashed with Madrid and club president Florentino Perez, commented on the debate on social media on Tuesday, while sharing an article which claimed "Real Madrid's enemies" were responsible for the team's struggles in LaLiga.

"The usual mouthpieces and the regime-aligned media are already spinning the same old narrative: the permanent conspiracy, Tebas posted on X. "When it isn't the Negreira case, it's the referee; or else, the complaint is that the official isn't an international-level referee."

"To maintain that referees are conspiring against Real Madrid is to live in another galaxy," Tebas continued. "That narrative serves as a smokescreen to hide other shortcomings that are plain to see in these opening matches of the season. It is easier to point to a conspiracy than to explain what is actually happening on the pitch.

"A refereeing error does not prove a conspiracy, nor does repeating the claim for years make it true. TIME TO TAKE OFF THE BLINDERS! It is only September, and they are already claiming the league is tainted. No one with common sense buys that old excuse anymore."

With seven games played, Madrid are already six points behind Barcelona, after losing at Real Betis and then in Sunday's derby.

- Jonathan David winner helps Atlético Madrid down Real Madrid

By contrast, Barça have maximum points, having scored 31 goals in seven matches.

Spain coach Luis de la Fuente -- who agreed a contract extension until 2032 on Monday -- was asked about the controversy on radio station Cadena Ser.

"I don't believe any of that," De la Fuente said, when asked about suggestions of a conspiracy. "If I believed in that, in such manipulation, I'd be better off going home, or we all would. And if someone believes it and has proof, then they should present that proof.

"But if we thought that, what would be the point? What would we be doing here? We'd just be wasting our time. That isn't my attitude towards life, or towards sport. I've lost, sometimes a lot, and I've won at other times. And I've never thought there was some hidden hand pulling the strings.

articles.headline: Wayne Rooney: 'Disappointing' if 'top player' JJ Gabriel leaves Man United
articles.description: Wayne Rooney has said it would be "disappointing" for Manchester United to lose "special talent" JJ Gabriel.
articles.body:
Wayne Rooney has said it would be "disappointing" for Manchester United to lose "special talent" JJ Gabriel.

Gabriel, 15, asked to leave United and Barcelona and Real Madrid are among the clubs monitoring his situation, sources told ESPN.

He turns 16 next month and recently shone on his UEFA Youth League debut against Sabah by scoring a hat trick.

"I have seen JJ grow up, he has been in [my son] Kai's team," Wayne Rooney told Stick To Football on Disney+. "Anyone close to it knew that was coming.

"In fairness to Manchester United they have done everything, absolutely everything, to keep him at the club.

"The club have treated him probably differently to the other players because he is such a special player. I know, I recognise that, because I was that player at Everton. I was getting that treatment at Everton.

"As a club, you need to do [it] to try to keep the better players.

"It's disappointing because he is such a top player and a lovely kid.

"You never know whether it's gone too far or whether there is a chance for him to stay."

United believe they could rectify the issue, sources previously told ESPN. 

- Why Man United's wantaway 15-year-old wonderkid, JJ Gabriel, is so highly rated

- Transfer rumors, news: Mesloub to replace Gabriel at Man United?

- Harry Maguire: Man United didn't take chances against Fulham, paid the price

Rooney became the Premier League's youngest goalscorer when he struck for Everton aged 16 years and 360 days old in 2002. That record is now held by Arsenal's Max Dowman after he scored against Everton in March aged 16 years and 73 days.

Rooney became a United and England legend and now sees an exciting talent within Gabriel.

"He is a top player," Rooney said of the 15-year-old. "His ability, his balance, he has shown he can go up the ages and score goals. The next step is first-team football where it's different, and you never know until you're in there.

"But he's such a special talent who understands the game really well.

"At some point this season he would [have] made his debut for the first-team, I'd imagine, so that's where it's disappointing."

articles.headline: Newcomers Jaylen Waddle, Jonah Coleman lead Broncos to win
articles.description: The Broncos mostly stood pat this offseason, keeping most of the 2025 roster together. But it was two newcomers on offense who helped them beat the Jaguars.
articles.body:
DENVER -- The Denver Broncos had a couple things atop their to-do list entering this past offseason. They wanted more impact at wide receiver and more production behind running back J.K. Dobbins. And the players they brought into fill both those needs -- veteran wide receiver Jaylen Waddle and rookie running back Jonah Coleman -- were integral in helping the Broncos (1-1) to their first win of the 2026 season.

"I'm proud of those guys," Broncos All-Pro left tackle Garett Bolles said. "That's why they're here, to do what they do."

In Denver's 20-13 victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday, Waddle finished with eight catches for 138 receiving yards, including a 49-yard catch in the second quarter and a key 29-yard reception on the Broncos' final, seal-the-win possession. And they asked Coleman to carry the running game when it was time to close out the Jaguars (1-1).

Waddle had the most receiving yards by a Bronco in a single game since Jerry Jeudy had 154 in the 2022 season finale. It was also the most receiving yards by a Broncos player in his home debut since Rick Upchurch had 153 in 1975.

"Significant, right?" Broncos coach Sean Payton said of Waddle's impact, for which the sixth-year receiver earned the game ball. "You can see the explosiveness, run after the catch. Glad he's ours."

Waddle's explosion came after a quiet Week 1 debut in which he had only one reception for 2 yards in a loss to the Kansas City Chiefs on "Monday Night Football." Sunday was exactly what the Broncos envisioned when they sent three draft picks, including a first-rounder, to the Miami Dolphins this past March to acquire the 27-year-old.

Payton said Sunday that Waddle's impact goes beyond stats because his explosiveness forces defenses to make decisions about when and where to bring more defenders to help on the receiver. The Broncos' only touchdown in their season-opening loss in Kansas City came when multiple defensive backs bracketed Waddle, leaving tight end Evan Engram open for a receiving score. The Broncos were able to isolate Waddle in several 1-on-1 match-ups Sunday, including the 49-yarder.

"They're a zone coverage team by nature, [but] we caught them in some man looks," Payton said. "... [Waddle] had one of those breakout games, it was great to see. He's kind of infectious, he doesn't have bad days, he likes football, he's a real good teammate. We needed it."

The Broncos also needed a spark in the running game on Sunday after Dobbins left in the third quarter with a left hamstring injury. Second-year running back RJ Harvey was already unavailable, also due to a hamstring injury. The Broncos struggled in the run game last season after Dobbins suffered a season-ending foot injury in Week 10, which caused Payton to search for a reserve running back with similar traits to Dobbins.

articles.headline: Titans trying to 'trust the process' after tough loss to Eagles
articles.description: The Titans could have a 1-1 record but they're 0-2 because they didn't finish on both sides of the ball down the stretch.
articles.body:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. --  Tennessee Titans defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons sat at his locker still in full uniform in disbelief almost 40 minutes after watching the Philadelphia Eagles celebrate Darius Cooper's game-winning, 3-yard touchdown reception with nine seconds left on the clock. These types of tough losses can send a team spiraling, especially a team like the Titans, who's 25.9-year-old average age is tied with the Green Bay Packers, Jacksonville Jaguars and New England Patriots for the fifth-youngest roster in the league. Titans coach Robert Saleh isn't a believer in moral victories, but he refuses to allow the 24-20 loss to the Eagles alter his approach.

"You can't let the result affect your process," Saleh said. "There is no good job in losing. You're either winning or you're losing. But you can't let that deter you from the process at which you attack it because that's the only chance you have to win a football game, having a great process."

The Titans could have a 1-1 record, but they're 0-2 because they didn't finish on either side of the ball down the stretch. 

Tennessee had a 73.7% win probability when Tyjae Spears' 27-yard run gave the Titans the first down while facing third-and-22. The Titans got the ball to Philadelphia's 9-yard line but had to settle for Joey Slye's 33-yard field goal to take a 20-17 lead with 1:56 left in the game. Tennessee's defense was unable to protect the lead, allowing Jalen Hurts to march the Eagles 65 yards to the end zone thanks to Cooper's catch.

"It's frustrating, for sure," Titans quarterback Cam Ward said. "We want to end every drive with a touchdown. That's our goal each and every time that we step on the field is to get a touchdown. And for us not to be able to help the defense in that situation, we take that upon ourselves"

The Titans hadn't won a game since last December. They were humiliated by Saleh's former team, the New York Jets in the season opener. Now the Titans have to figure out a way to flush the bad feelings after having a win snatched from their grasp.

Second-year receiver Elic Ayomanor is taking a trust the process approach to get ready for the next game, which will be on the road against the New York Giants on Sunday. Ayomanor's faith is in the hard work he put in during the offseason and what he's going to do leading up to the game. That hard work has made Ayomanor a player Saleh referenced when asked how the Titans can weather the storm of a two-game losing streak to start the season.

Saleh said that everyone would be sick once they sat down and watched the film from the loss. The film showed exactly what Saleh thought he'd see, a failure to execute in multiple phases late in the game. But there were also plenty of shortcomings throughout the day. The Eagles were able to convert a ridiculous 11 of their 18 third-down opportunities. articles.headline: Nicolas Batum announces retirement after 18 NBA seasons
articles.description: Nicolas Batum has announced his retirement after 18 NBA seasons. A mainstay of the French national team, Batum played most of his NBA career with the Clippers, Hornets and Blazers.
articles.headlineJa: ニコラ・バトゥムがNBA18シーズンのキャリアを経て現役引退を発表
articles.descriptionJa: ニコラ・バトゥムがNBAで18シーズンプレーした後に現役引退を発表しました。フランス代表の主力であったバトゥムは、NBAキャリアの大部分をクリッパーズ、ホーネッツ、ブレイザーズで過ごしました。

articles.headline: Doc Rivers joins NBC as analyst, says coaching career over
articles.description: Doc Rivers turned down an offer to become an NBA analyst for NBC after retiring as a player in 1996 because he couldn't promise then-NBC Sports chairman Dick Ebersol that he wouldn't become a coach.
articles.headlineJa: ドック・リバースがアナリストとしてNBCに加入、監督キャリアの終了を表明
articles.descriptionJa: ドック・リバースは1996年に選手引退後、当時のNBCスポーツ会長ディック・エバーソルに「コーチにならない」と約束できなかったため、NBCのNBAアナリスト就任要請を断っていました。

articles.headline: Clippers name lawyer John Gibson interim governor
articles.description: Los Angeles-based trial lawyer John Gibson will serve as the Clippers' interim governor. He will take over for Steve Ballmer, who has been suspended one year following an investigation into salary cap circumvention.
articles.headlineJa: クリッパーズ、弁護士のジョン・ギブソンを暫定オーナー（ガバナー）に指名
articles.descriptionJa: ロサンゼルスを拠点とする法廷弁護士のジョン・ギブソンが、クリッパーズの暫定ガバナーに就任します。サラリーキャップ回避の調査を受けて1年間の停職処分となったスティーブ・バルマーの後任を務めます。
